newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MARCH 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MARCH 28.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Institutional changes are under way by the authorities of the capital market, with the aim of making speculation on the stock market a thing of the past and creating the prerequisites for the introduction of new products.

--Fiscal developments ovr the past few months have improved the prospects of a positive evaluation of Greece's credit rating on foreign and internal market, Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis said yesterday, following Standard & Poors positive report.

--The sale of 6,500 state-held properties and resolution of property disputes with the state, were announced by Deputy Finance Minister George Drys yesterday as part of the state's efforts to boost revenues and meet budget targets.

--The calm waters of the Athens Stock Exchange has finally forced the Bank of Greece to reduce rates in the interbank market, with immediate effects: interbank rates are up to 2.0 percent down while the climate has been further bolstered by Christodoulakis's firm belief that the central bank's new strategies in money markets will lead to a further fall in interest rates of state titles.
--Tight controls on ministry budgets will be a fact of life from now on, with audits being conducted every three months by the General Accounting Office, in an effort to keep a lid on spending.
--Alpha Creit Bank yesterday announced plans to raise an impressive 72.6 billion drachmas from its share capital increase.

--Despite a slight improvement in March, tax inflows for the state are still short of budget targets and the finance ministry is reportedly considering changes at the managerial level at tax offices to get inflows moving again. The figures will be used to judge managers' performances at the beginning of May.
--The Bank of Greece says the situation on the interbank market is under control as is, subsequently, the conditions of stability of the drachma.
--Terms for the sale of Cretabank are significantly more elastic than previously, following agreement by the national economy and finance ministries and the Bank of the Greece.
--Tax declarations may be submitted by Monday, the finance ministry decided yesterday, after agreeing to extend the Friday deadline.
